cpg_region: promoter region upstream exon IV; PC1 composite of 4 CpG sites (specific CpGs not identified in main text, see Supplementary Table 1, not available); 11 candidate CpGs span chr11:27723096-27723219
intervention_detail: Maternal trait anxiety (STAI-T) during pregnancy as proxy for chronic prenatal stress, assessed postpartum; effect conditional on residential green space exposure (300m buffer around prenatal address)
method: targeted bisulfite PCR + NGS (Illumina NextSeq500); PCA-derived composite (varimax rotation, 4 CpGs, 22.4% variance explained); simple slope analysis following significant moderation
quality_notes: GxE/moderation design, not a direct stress-methylation association: overall main effect of maternal anxiety on BDNF DNAm was NOT significant (beta=0.06, p=.53); direction and p-value reported here are for the SIGNIFICANT SIMPLE SLOPE at low (-1SD) green space exposure only. At high (+1SD) green space, slope was non-significant and opposite in sign (beta=-0.18, p=.17) — not coded as 'mixed' since this slope carries no significant evidence, per convention also used for Rivera_2024. Interaction term itself: beta=-0.28, p=.008 (this is the moderation p-value, distinct from the association p-value used above). Effect specific to 300m buffer; not significant at 500m (p=.06) or 1000m (p=.09), though direction consistent. PC2 (3 CpGs) showed no significant main or interactive effects — see separate null row. Cross-sectional at birth; maternal anxiety measured postpartum as proxy for prenatal trait (high test-retest stability, r=.86, cited to justify this proxy). Analytic n fluctuates ~105-109 across models (N=3 outliers >3SD excluded); enrolled cohort n=110. Scope note: central finding is an environmental moderator (green space) of the anxiety-methylation link, not a direct unconditional stress-methylation association.

intervention_detail: Maternal prenatal depressive symptoms (EPDS>=10 vs <10) assessed 2nd/3rd trimester; TRANSGENERATIONAL DESIGN - exposure measured in mother, methylation measured in infant buccal cells at ~2 months postnatal age; no significant sex interaction (both sexes affected)
method: bisulfite pyrosequencing (PyroMark Q24)
quality_notes: Mean methylation across 5 CpGs decreased with maternal depression exposure (b=-2.590). Effect driven primarily by CpG3, adjacent to CREB binding site (b=-3.244, p=.002 at single-CpG level). Direction is OPPOSITE to prior animal literature on prenatal stress and Bdnf IV (which shows hypermethylation) - authors flag this as a notable species/direction discrepancy worth citing in your Discussion. Maternal cortisol did NOT predict this effect (both stressor-response and diurnal AUC cortisol non-significant), suggesting depression effect is not glucocorticoid-mediated.

intervention_detail: ACUTE laboratory-induced psychosocial stress (Trier Social Stress Test); within-subject repeated measures at pre-stress, 10min post-stress, and 90min follow-up; NOT chronic stress/trauma - single acute stressor design; NO unstressed control group
method: bisulfite PCR + Sequenom EpiTYPER (MassARRAY)
quality_notes: No significant overall effect of sampling time on mean BDNF methylation (F(2,1098)=1.31 p=.271; blood-cell-adjusted F(2,1523)=0.87 p=.418). 1 of 10 individual CpG units showed a significant time effect but did not survive at region-mean level. Cohort is elderly (age 61-67, born 1942-1947) with high likelihood of early WWII-related adversity exposure - population confound to note. CONSIDER: this is acute stress reactivity, a different construct from the chronic stress/trauma studies dominating this dataset's stress arm - may warrant exclusion or a separate acute-stress flag rather than pooling with trauma studies for the directional-consistency analysis. Companion finding in same paper (OXTR1 hypermethylation post-stress, p<.001) is OUT OF SCOPE - not one of the three target genes.
